status: DESIGN (Task 043). Code detection is implemented in Task 045; until then the maker AI names the type and this file tells every section what that type needs.
source: Navin's five points (22 Oct 2026); Vision Spec 'Agreed on 21 October 2026'; rulebook vision-2026-10-21 (S1-06, S3-*, S6-03, S7-01, S7-02); docs/roadmap/TARAZU.md
how_it_is_used: Section 1 (understanding) gives every teachable item one content type; the code-side hints below let BIE propose a type before the AI reads the page and flag a disagreement.
The type decides which teacher questions are required (S1-06), the teaching pattern of the lesson, the video blocks of the director, the game mechanic (S6-03) and the notes infographic (S7-02).
One item has one primary type; a whole section of a chapter can mix types. Examples, PYQs and headings are roles, not types: an example takes the type of what it illustrates.
Changing a type, a required question or a pattern is a rule change: bump the version, record why, and rerun the locked test set.

kya.meaning: what it is, what it is about

kyun.meaning: why it is so, why it matters

kab.meaning: when, in what order, under what conditions

kaun.meaning: who does it, to whom, which one

kahan.meaning: where it is found or happens

legacy_types._note: The Section 1 schema of 21 Oct 2026 (bie/brain/understanding.py CONTENT_TYPES) maps onto these types as follows; Task 045 switches the schema to the ids below.
legacy_types.example: role: takes the type of what it illustrates
legacy_types.question: role: a PYQ or exercise, linked to the items it tests
legacy_types.other: none: Section 1 must say why no type fits

types.name: Process
types.what_it_is: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law).

typical_questions.question: What is the process and what does it achieve?
How does it happen, step by step?
In what order, and under which conditions does each step happen?
Where does each step take place?
Why is each step needed, and what goes wrong if one is missing?
What is the final result or product?

teaching_pattern: each step with its cause and its condition
what breaks when a step fails
the whole run once more at speed

game_mechanic.how: The student runs the process step by step; a wrong step visibly breaks it and says why.

structure: numbered or lettered list of actions
arrows between boxes in a figure

code_checks: at least two ordered steps
every step names what changes
a 'how' question exists (S1-06)

types.name: Structure
types.what_it_is: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament).

typical_questions.question: What are its parts?
Where is each part, and where is the whole found?
How does the shape of each part suit its job?
Why is it built this way?
Which part does which job?

teaching_pattern: zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside)
function of each part tied to its shape

game_mechanic.how: The student builds the structure; it only works when every part is in the right place, and a wrong part shows the failure it causes.

structure: a list of parts with functions

code_checks: every labelled part in the figure is an item
every part has a function or a reason it is named

types.name: Classification
types.what_it_is: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs).

typical_questions.question: What is being divided, and into which kinds?
On what basis is it divided?
How does each kind differ from the others?
What are examples of each kind?
Where is each kind found?

teaching_pattern: the tree from the top down
each kind with its identifying feature and an example

game_mechanic.how: The student sorts real specimens or cases by their features; a wrong sort shows which feature was misread.

structure: a heading followed by sub-headings of the same level
a table whose first column lists kinds

code_checks: the basis is stated
every kind has an identifying feature
a 'compare' or 'difference' question exists (S1-06)

types.name: Comparison
types.what_it_is: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).

typical_questions.question: On which points are they compared?
Where do they differ, point by point?
What do they have in common?
Why does each difference exist?
Which example shows the difference best?

teaching_pattern: criteria one at a time, both sides together
the most confused pair named directly

game_mechanic.how: The student meets a case and must decide which side it belongs to by its features; a wrong call shows the feature that decides.

structure: a two- or three-column table with criteria rows

code_checks: at least two sides and one criterion
each criterion filled for every side
a 'compare' or 'difference' question exists (S1-06)

types.name: Timeline
types.what_it_is: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory).

typical_questions.question: When did each event happen, and in what order?
Who acted, and on whom?
Where did it happen?
Why did it happen then: the conditions and the atmosphere?
What changed because of it?

teaching_pattern: events in order with their causes

game_mechanic.how: The student acts as a person of the time; a wrong choice breaks the timeline and shows what really happened and why.

code_checks: dates are in order and match the book
each event has a when (S1-06)
reasoning/chronology checks from bie/reasoning (chronology_reasoning, event_order_reasoning)

types.name: Reasoning (cause and effect)
types.what_it_is: Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed).

typical_questions.question: Why does it happen: what is the cause?
How does the cause lead to the effect, link by link?
What follows from it?
What evidence shows the link?
When does the link not hold?

teaching_pattern: each link of the chain with its mechanism

game_mechanic.how: The student changes the cause and predicts the effect, or finds the broken link that caused a wrong outcome.

structure: a sentence with a connective of cause

code_checks: every chain has a cause, a link and an effect
no cycle in the cause graph (bie/reasoning causal_graph, graph_cycles)
a 'why' and a 'how' question exist

types.name: Facts and numbers
types.what_it_is: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma).

typical_questions.question: What exactly is the fact or value, with its unit?
Compared with what is it big or small?
Where does the number come from, and when was it true?
Why does this number matter here?

teaching_pattern: the number shown to scale against something familiar
where it comes from (book or outside, dated)
a formula built term by term when there is one

game_mechanic.how: The student estimates or sets the value and sees it to scale; a wrong guess shows how far off it was and why.

structure: a sentence with a number and a unit

code_checks: the value and unit match the book exactly
unit and number checks from bie/math_intelligence (unit_parser, unit_mismatch, numerical_equivalence)
outside numbers carry a source and a date

types.name: Figure
types.what_it_is: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only).

typical_questions.question: What does the figure show, part by part?
Which label points to which part?
How should a student read it (axes, arrows, colours, scale)?
Why is it in the book: what does it prove or explain?

teaching_pattern: what the figure is and why it is here
a reading path across it (labels in order)
the one thing to remember from it
link back to the text it explains
types.visual_grammar: the original figure or a licensed better asset (bie/brain/assets.py); figure_semantics and diagram_classification in bie/document_intelligence as checks

game_mechanic.how: The student labels or rebuilds the figure; a wrong label shows what that part really is.

structure: a page region with an image and little or no native text

code_checks: every visible label is an item with a parent figure (S1-03)
image-only items are marked source=image
the figure is linked to the text items it explains

types.name: Definition
types.what_it_is: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty).

typical_questions.question: What does the term mean, in the book's words?
What does each key word of the definition add?
What is a clear example and a near non-example?
Why is this term needed in the chapter?

teaching_pattern: the book's definition word by word
a non-example that tests the boundary
where the term is used next in the chapter
types.visual_grammar: term card; concept map link to its parent concept

game_mechanic.how: The student decides whether cases fit the definition; a wrong call shows which word of the definition decides.

structure: a bold or italic term followed by its meaning

code_checks: the book's exact words are kept
an example exists
outside wording is marked basis=outside
